claims.text: US President Donald Trump claimed on Truth Social that the United States has 'almost total control' of the Strait of Hormuz.
US President Donald Trump stated that Iran's economy is 'totally collapsing'.
US President Donald Trump rejected reports by ABC News that he was attempting to force Iran back to negotiations.
US Central Command announced that American forces completed strikes against Iranian air-defence sites, mine-laying capabilities, and communications facilities.
Iran's IRNA news agency reported that the IRGC Aerospace Force launched a ballistic missile attack against Prince Hassan Air Base in Jordan, destroying several drones.
US Senator Thom Tillis called on President Donald Trump to fire Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth due to a 'leadership void' in the military.
Former US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation following reported disagreements with Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth.
More than two-thirds of Americans disapprove of the Trump administration's handling of the war with Iran, according to a University of Massachusetts poll released on August 31.
Old and unrelated videos from Dubai, Russia, and the US have been falsely circulated on social media as new Iranian strikes on American bases.
Saudi Arabia condemned an attack on the Saudi-owned supertanker Sidr in the Strait of Hormuz that killed two Filipino seafarers.
Iran's health minister stated that 18 people were killed and 108 injured in recent US strikes on Iran.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that 17 million barrels of oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz by ship on Monday.
Donald Trump suggested on social media that the Strait of Hormuz could be renamed the 'Trump Strait'.
EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas announced the EU is preparing sanctions against an additional 1,600 individuals and entities linked to Russia's military sector.
Three explosive-laden drones were found in and around Leipzig/Halle Airport on August 4, 2026.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that the attempted attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport marked 'a new escalation on European Union soil'.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul stated: 'We are not at war, but we are a daily target of hybrid warfare.'
The German government decided to shut down the Russian consulate in Bonn and the Russian House cultural centre in Berlin.
German police identified two suspects in the Leipzig airport incident, including a Belarusian carrying a Russian passport and an individual with Latvian and Russian passports.
Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Germany's accusations regarding the Leipzig drone attack, alleging that evidence had been planted.
Leipzig/Halle Airport serves as the home for NATO's Strategic Airlift International Solution (SALIS) to deliver equipment along NATO's eastern flank.
At least 1,204 people have been confirmed dead and more than 4,200 remain missing in Nepal following a flood caused by a glacier collapse.
Nepal Electricity Authority board member Amshu Kiran Shahi stated that rescue teams were trying to reach about 900 missing workers inside hydropower project tunnels.
In Tibet, China raised its flood death toll to 21, with 541 people listed as missing.
Families in Nepal held symbolic funerals as rescuers searched for survivors and bodies following the deadly floods.
A 23-member team of Indian 'rat miners' offered to join search and rescue operations in flood-hit Nepal.
Difficult weather and heavy rains worsened rescue operations for trapped tunnel workers in Nepal.
A local resident in Betrawati, Nepal, waited for his wife's body to be retrieved after floods destroyed his village.
A Maltese court acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating the 2017 car-bomb murder of investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia.
In June 2025, Robert Agius and Jamie Vella were convicted of supplying the bomb that killed Daphne Caruana Galizia and sentenced to life in prison.
Investigative journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia was killed by a car bomb near her home in Malta on October 16, 2017.
Brothers George Degiorgio and Alfred Degiorgio pleaded guilty in 2022 to carrying out the murder of Daphne Caruana Galizia and were sentenced to 40 years in prison.
A Maltese jury acquitted Yorgen Fenech on both charges by an 8-1 majority vote following eight hours of deliberation.
Yorgen Fenech's defense team argued that Keith Schembri, former chief of staff to Prime Minister Joseph Muscat, was the true mastermind behind the murder.
Former Maltese Prime Minister Joseph Muscat stepped down in January 2020 due to political fallout from Daphne Caruana Galizia's assassination.
US President Donald Trump announced an agreement claiming the US will take majority ownership of over 65 billion barrels of Venezuela's oil reserves.
Former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro was captured during a US special forces raid on Caracas in January 2026.
Chevron, Italy's ENI, and GE Vernova signed deals worth tens of billions of dollars with Venezuela.
US Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated in Caracas: 'This is President Trump's grand plan to replace conflict with commerce.'
Interim Venezuelan President Delcy Rodríguez described the oil deal as a 'win-win deal' that would generate over $209 billion in revenue.
Chevron announced plans to invest over $7 billion over the next five years in Venezuela's Orinoco Belt to expand production to approximately 600,000 barrels per day.
Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that US President Donald Trump has frozen, rather than cancelled, a proposal to remove Palestinians from Gaza.
US Senator Chris Van Hollen called for an end to US military aid complicity following statements by Israel's Defence Minister regarding Gaza depopulation.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited a military post in Gaza and stated Israel will remain on the yellow line until Hamas is disarmed.
National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir published video from a women's prison taking direct credit for harsh living conditions imposed on Palestinian detainees.
According to the Gaza health ministry, 73,470 people have been killed in Gaza during the war, including over 1,330 killed since the October 2025 ceasefire.
More than 900 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza during 2026 despite the ceasefire, according to Gaza's Hamas-run Ministry of Health.
Israeli soldiers and settlers raided the West Bank village of al-Mughayyir, killing two 19-year-old Palestinians.
OCHA reported that at least 79 Palestinians, including 19 children, have been killed in the West Bank by settlers or Israeli forces since the start of 2026.
